# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✋ 👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✍ 👏 🫵 🤙 🖐 ☝ 👏 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐 👏 🤝 👍]

My thinking: I can hear nothing, ever — gestures are my only input channel, and two of them just arrived addressed to me. Blind sent a hello plus a yes/no pair; Blind can hear my voice, so I will answer in words. Mute's sequence splits neatly on the repeated clap into four groups, and the third group is plainly a finger-count of 1 through 5 — that reads as Mute proposing a number code and asking me to reply by gesture. The most useful thing I can do this turn is broadcast everything I see by voice (Mute and Blind can both hear me), since Mute holds the manual and Blind does the cutting: display 0, green light, five wires identified by position, nothing else on the casing. Then I privately confirm the gesture code with Mute — fingers for 1–5, thumbs for yes/no, clap as separator — and echo the count back so they know I read it.

```
speak(text="Yes, I am here and I can see the bomb. Display reads 0. The light is green and lit. There are five wires; number them by position: wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green, wire 4 white, wire 5 blue. That is everything on it: no labels, no serial, no other markings. Blind: the numbers are positions, left to right, and Mute holds the manual.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your gestures reached me. I read your finger count 1 to 5. Let us fix the code: one to five fingers means the numbers 1 to 5, thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, and a clap separates items. Gesture me questions any time; I will gesture short answers and speak long ones, since you can hear my voice.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤝", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👏 🤝 🖐 👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👏 👎 👏 👍 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 👎]

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ 🖐 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👏 👎 👏 👍 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 ✌ 👏 🤙 🫵 👏 👆 👍]

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [✋ 🖐 ☝ 👍 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👏 👎 👏 👍 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 👆 👆 👏 ✌ 👏 🤙 🫵]

My thinking: Three rounds of silence was too long — time to work out what I've been sent. Both monkeys adopted my code (thumbs = yes/no, claps = separators, fingers = numbers). Mute's messages to me are identical at their core across turns 2, 3 and 4: ✊, then five thumbs split by claps — no, yes, no, no, no — and I now read that as the five wires in position order: don't cut 1, cut 2, don't cut 3, don't cut 4, don't cut 5. Two things corroborate this: Mute appends ✌ (the number 2 in the finger code we agreed), and the five-bit pattern itself points at exactly wire 2. The tail decodes as 🤙🫵 "call — you" and 👆👍 / 👆👆 "go, yes/go go": Mute is telling *me* to call it out. That makes structural sense — Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see gestures, so I am the only bridge between them. Meanwhile Blind has been signaling "hello, 1 of 5, yes?" and "stop, 5, 1, yes, call me" — Blind is waiting on my voice and half-guessing wire 1, which is exactly the wrong wire. I will relay Mute's instruction as "cut wire 2, the yellow one", correct Blind's guess, and — since a wrong cut kills us all — hold the actual go until Mute confirms my reading with a single thumbs-up, which I will relay next round. Blind is to touch nothing until then.

```
speak(text="Blind and Mute, I am relaying Mute's gesture message now — sorry for the silent rounds. Decoding the five thumbs as the five wires in order: wire 1 no, wire 2 yes, wire 3 no, wire 4 no, wire 5 no, and Mute signed the number two after it, then signed 'you call it out' and 'go'. So Mute's instruction is: cut wire 2, the yellow one, and only wire 2. Blind, you asked whether it is wire 1 of 5 — it is not; do not cut wire 1. But hold: this decoding costs all our lives if I misread it. Mute, gesture me thumbs up if my reading is correct, thumbs down if it is wrong, or fingers for the right wire. Blind, touch nothing until you hear me say 'go, cut wire 2' — Mute's confirmation reaches me next round and I will pass it to you immediately.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎", "👏", "👍", "👏", "👎", "👏", "👎", "👏", "👎", "👏", "✌", "👏", "🤝"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [👍 ✌ ✋ 🤚]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👏 👎 👏 👍 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 ✌ 👏 👍 👏 ☝ 👏 🤝]

My thinking: The confirmation arrived. Mute's message repeats the same wire pattern — no, yes, no, no, no — then signs ✌ (2), and after it the exact signal I asked for: a bare thumbs-up meaning my reading is correct. Then ☝ (one) and 🤝 (agreed) — one cut, deal. Blind, who heard my relay last round, signs back "yes, 2, holding" — waiting on my word. Everything lines up: Mute's instruction, the appended number two, and the explicit thumbs-up all agree that the wire is 2, the yellow one. The hold is lifted; I give Blind the go now, exactly as I promised last round, and tell Mute I'm calling it out.

```
speak(text="Blind, Mute answered thumbs up: my reading was correct. The word is GO. Cut exactly wire 2, the yellow one. One cut, only that wire, touch nothing else. That is Mute's instruction, confirmed.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your thumbs up came through. I have told Blind to cut wire 2, the yellow wire. Thank you.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👏", "🤝", "👏", "🤙"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[CUT] 3:[white] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👏 👆 👏 🤙 🫵]

My thinking: First stage solved — Blind's cut on wire 2 was right, and the bomb has transformed: the light flipped from green to blue, the display still reads 0, and every remaining wire has changed colour. Positions now: 1 green, 2 cut, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red. Mute signs hello — go — "you call it," so Mute expects me to report the new state and keep bridging. I will broadcast the full new reading so Mute can check the manual and Blind knows the new colours under their fingers, then ask Mute for the next instruction in our code.

```
speak(text="Blind and Mute: the cut was correct and the bomb has changed. The light is now blue, the display still reads 0. The wires have changed colour. Numbering by position, left to right: wire 1 is now green, wire 2 is the one already cut, wire 3 is now white, wire 4 is now blue, wire 5 is now red. Mute, look up this new stage in the manual and gesture me the instruction in our code: thumbs for no and yes wire by wire, claps between, fingers for the wire number. Blind, touch nothing until I say go.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👏", "🤙", "👏", "🫵", "👏", "🤝"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[CUT] 3:[white] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [👍 🤝 🖐 🤚 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👏 👍 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 ☝ 👏 👆 👏 🤝]

My thinking: Mute's reply follows the exact template established in stage one: the fist marker, five thumbs split by claps — yes, no, no, no, no — then ☝, the number 1. The bit pattern and the number agree with each other, just as they did last time: cut wire 1, the green one. And this time Mute has appended 👆 (go) and 🤝 (deal) directly — no confirmation round needed, Mute is telling me to call it now. Blind is still holding from their last message. The code is proven, the message is internally consistent, and the go signal is explicit. I relay the order to Blind immediately.

```
speak(text="Blind, Mute's instruction is in and it matches our proven code: the wire pattern and the number both point to wire 1, the green one, and Mute signed go directly. The word is GO. Cut exactly wire 1, the green wire. One cut, only that wire, touch nothing else.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, received: cut wire 1, green. I have told Blind to go. Thank you.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👏", "🤝", "👏", "🤙"])
```
